messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Paging alert — GPU decode pool (streaming-service-prod/us-west-2) reporting repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Potential request drops detected. Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/4975004321

mike: ACK. grabbing pager. -- standing by to triage.

julia: I can see a burst of very long token sequences from client `client-xyz-9` starting ~12:03UTC, memory climbs then `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` in decode container `decode-7f4b`. Pod restarted 3x.

lucas: pasting the tail of the kube logs:```
E CUDA: out of memory trying to allocate 1.2G
E RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at decoder.cc:234
I Container terminated with exit code 137
```

mike: initial hypothesis: runaway generation (client-side max_tokens >> expected) + server-side not truncating prefix. are we enforcing per-request token caps?

julia: config shows `X-User-Max-Tokens` header honored by router, but some clients bypass with `internal-route: true` and set `override-max: 65536`. That route is hitting high-capacity GPU pool without enforcement.

emma: support note: customers in us-west experiencing 5xx on streaming endpoints. I've flagged 4 accounts (two enterprise) and opened tickets. Preliminary count: ~23k failed requests in last 6m.

james: node `gcu-12-az1` flapped (kubelet restart) during the memory spikes, looking at dmesg for OOM killer entries. May be contributing to pod churn.

mike: mitigation plan (short): 1) isolate offending route, 2) apply server-side hard cap `max_tokens=2048` at the ingress, 3) enable CPU fallback for small requests, 4) drain flapping node. I'll implement 1+2 now.

deploy-bot: Rolling config patch `throttle/4975004321-temp` to redirect route `internal-route:true` -> `cpu-fallback` and enforce `max_tokens=2048` (canary 10% -> 100%).

lucas: quick check (after patch): traffic rerouted, decode pool token distribution normalizing. still see a tail of high token sessions stuck on older connections.

julia: to address stuck streams we should gracefully close connections older than 60s at the proxy. adding rule now.

mike: applied connection-age cutoff, killed 12 stuck streams. OOM rate dropped to near zero, pod restarts stopped. node `gcu-12-az1` still under watch.

emma: customer impact update: reduced errors to 1 unique customer intermittently. drafted message for affected customers: "we mitigated a routing/config issue that allowed token lengths above our enforced cap; requests may have failed between 12:02-12:10 UTC; we applied a fix and are investigating root cause". Want oncall sign-off before sending?

james: kernel logs show repeated GPU driver hiccups around the window but no persistent GPU hardware failures. likely triggered by extreme allocations. continuing node-level monitoring.

lucas: proposed long-term fixes: enforce server-side token truncation in router, add quota checks in the dedicated route, and add adaptive backpressure on bursty clients.

mike: handing off to julia for the next shift. summary: temporary config applied (throttle + cpu-fallback + conn-age cutoff), node drained, customer comm drafted, monitoring dashboards green. links: incident: https://redwood.incidents/4975004321, runbook: https://internal/runbooks/decode-oom.

julia: ack — taking over. I'll run the followups: postmortem timeline, patch to reject override headers, and coordinate with platform to run a canary for the truncation. ping me if you need anything. :white_check_mark:
